children: Benchmark indices opened lower on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, dragged by selling in information technology and metals stocks, even as fast-moving consumer goods and defence counters held firm. The BSE Sensex, which closed at 73,606.75 on Monday, opened at 73,484.38 and was trading at 73,276.08 at 9.20 am, down 330.67 points or 0.45 per cent. The NSE Nifty50, which ended Monday's session at 22,753.20, opened at 22,708.80 and fell to 22,671.25, a loss of 81.95 points or 0.36 per cent as of 9.20 am.

Tuesday marks the monthly derivatives expiry on the NSE, a factor widely expected to amplify intraday swings. "With monthly expiry today, extreme volatility is expected, and sharp intraday swings could dominate market action...traders should avoid chasing the initial gap-down and remain selective," said Gaurav Udani, Founder of ThinCredBlu Securities.

Among the Nifty50 top gainers in early trade, Tata Consumer Products led with a rise of 3.04 per cent to ₹965.00 against its previous close of ₹936.50. Bharat Electronics (BEL) gained 1.35 per cent to ₹367.90 from ₹363.00, while Max Healthcare rose 1.25 per cent to ₹845.40 from ₹835.00. BSE Limited advanced 0.99 per cent to ₹3,392.20 from ₹3,359.00, and Shriram Finance edged up 0.70 per cent to ₹830.75 from ₹825.00.

On the losing side, Infosys was the top loser, shedding 2.51 per cent to ₹1,136.70 from its previous close of ₹1,166.00. JSW Steel declined 1.40 per cent to ₹1,242.30 from ₹1,260.00, Asian Paints dropped 1.28 per cent to ₹2,292.20 from ₹2,322.00, and TCS slipped 1.15 per cent to ₹2,505.80 from ₹2,535.00.

The weakness in IT stocks came despite Wall Street's overnight gains, driven in part by Anthropic's IPO filing on Nasdaq that fuelled a rally in semiconductor stocks. The Dow Jones rose 0.3 per cent, the S&P 500 gained 0.7 per cent, and the Nasdaq advanced 0.8 per cent on Monday. "The strength in US technology shares should be treated as a global sentiment cue rather than a direct signal for Indian IT...domestic technology stocks will remain more sensitive to quarterly guidance, deal pipelines, client spending and margins," said Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder and CEO of HST Wealth.

Crude oil remains a persistent overhang, with Brent hovering near $115 per barrel amid ongoing West Asian tensions and attacks on Saudi infrastructure. "Brent crude remaining above $114 and the US 10-year bond yield hovering around 4.97 per cent continue to be near-term headwinds for the market...the improving fundamentals of the corporate sector as reflected in Q2 earnings and the robust domestic fund inflows will continue to support the market," said Dr V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments.

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) remained net sellers on Monday, offloading equities worth ₹1,462 crore. Domestic institutional investors (DIIs), however, extended their buying streak to 10 consecutive sessions, purchasing equities worth ₹2,609 crore. The Indian rupee closed at 95.19 against the US dollar on Monday, down 25 paise for the third straight session.

The US Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting, which begins Tuesday, is a key event, with the central bank widely expected to hold rates at 3.75–4 per cent. "Guidance on inflation will matter more than the widely expected unchanged rate decision...a hawkish signal could lift yields and the dollar and restrict emerging-market flows," Radhakrishnan added.

Shrikant Chouhan, Head of Equity Research at Kotak Neo, said 22,600 on the Nifty and 73,000 on the Sensex now form the first critical support.a sustained breakout above this resistance could open the way towards 23,000/74,500," he said.

Six Nifty constituents — Bajaj Auto, Cipla, Larsen and Toubro, Maruti Suzuki, SBI Life Insurance and Tata Steel — are scheduled to report their September quarter results on Tuesday, which could further influence market direction through the session.

title: Expiry day nerves: Sensex, Nifty open in red as IT drags; FMCG, Defence buck the trend
